t: The Secretary of Defense may establish or develop installations and facilities which he determines to be vital to the security of the United States, and in connection therewith to acquire, construct, convert, rehabilitate, or install permanent or temporary public works, including land acquisition, site preparation, appurtenances, utilities, and equipment in the total amount of $150,000,000: Provided, That the Secretary of Defense, or his designee, shall notify the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives, immediately upon reaching a final decision to implement, of the cost of construction of any public work undertaken under this section, including real estate actions pertaining thereto.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the notification requirement is a form of consultation, but it runs only to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. It also happens after the Secretary of Defense has reached a final decision, so nobody is consulted beforehand. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is involved in the decision to establish the installations.
fable.s: shall notify the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives, immediately upon reaching a final decision to implement

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to notify congressional committees after a decision has been made. Congress is considered part of the federal government, so this is an intra-governmental notification, not participation by outside parties. The definition explicitly excludes reports to or notifications of Congress.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Defense, or his designee, shall notify the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives, immediately upon reaching a final decision to implement, of the cost of construction of any public work undertaken under this section

opus.w: The only procedural requirement is a notice to congressional committees, and that happens after the final decision is made. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so this is not participation. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing or allowed to object.
opus.s: the Secretary of Defense, or his designee, shall notify the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives, immediately upon reaching a final decision to implement

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to notify congressional committees about construction costs. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Notification to internal government bodies does not constitute participation by outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: Provided, That the Secretary of Defense, or his designee, shall notify the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives, immediately upon reaching a final decision to implement, of the cost of construction of any public work undertaken under this section
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying Congress constitutes "participation" because it involves an external check on executive power. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, reporting to Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation by outside parties.
